Industry 4.0 is a blend of the hyper-connected digital world of Information Technology (IT) and Operational Technology (OT) in manufacturing.
Smart manufacturing integrates manufacturing assets with sensors, computing platforms, communication technology, data-intensive modeling, control, simulation, and predictive engineering.
The digital thread refers to the communication framework of a connected data flow with an integrated view of an asset's data lifecycle and functional perspectives, from design to manufacture.
Cyber threats to smart manufacturing enterprises can be motivated by espionage, financial gain, or other reasons to compromise data confidentiality, integrity, and availability.
Additive manufacturing (3D printing) introduces new cybersecurity challenges around the protection of intellectual property (IP) related to 3D object designs and manufacturing parameters.
Remote attestation is a mechanism to verify the integrity of a system's software configuration and detect any unintended or malicious modifications.
Swarm attestation is an efficient approach to collectively verify the software integrity of all devices in a smart manufacturing system.

Cloud manufacturing allows manufacturing enterprises to utilize well-established resources and capabilities, such as Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), over the internet, but introduces new cybersecurity challenges.
RFID and smart devices in the supply chain can provide bidirectional communication and sensor data, but also expose the system to potential attacks if not properly secured.
Watermarking can be used to uniquely identify actors and protect intellectual property in outsourced additive manufacturing processes.
The confidentiality of sensitive data, such as manufacturing processes, cost information, operational data, and intellectual property, must be protected in smart manufacturing.
The integrity of smart manufacturing systems is crucial to prevent malicious modifications, such as the introduction of backdoors, unauthorized access to protected memory, and hardware tampering.
Availability is a fundamental requirement for cyber-physical production systems (CPPS) in smart manufacturing, as any system failures or disruptions can lead to physical damage or harm.
The increasing degree of automation and system autonomy in smart manufacturing will raise the importance of human and machine safety.
The convergence of IT and OT in Industry 4.0 introduces new cybersecurity challenges, as traditional data security practices may not be sufficient to protect the integrated cyber-physical systems.
